architecture.goal: Scale the current phase-2 architecture to a defendable 1M+ daily workload by replacing monolithic daily selection with distributed slot-based dispatch across 24 hours, while preserving the existing downstream flow from SQS FIFO into the orchestrator, Step Functions, and consumer.
runtime_shape: Pending records are stored with dispatch metadata for a specific day and a computed dispatch slot.
EventBridge Scheduler invokes the dispatch Lambda repeatedly across a 24-hour window using one schedule per dispatch slot.
Each dispatch Lambda invocation reads only one date-slot partition from DynamoDB instead of scanning the entire daily workload.
The dispatch Lambda publishes records to SQS FIFO using SendMessageBatch with MessageGroupId bound to provider identity.
SQS FIFO High Throughput mode automatically partitions traffic by MessageGroupId hash while preserving in-group ordering.
The existing orchestrator Lambda, state machine, and consumer Lambda remain unchanged in responsibility and integration shape after a message enters the queue.
explicit_non_goals: Manual shuffle-sharding or custom shard routing in application code.
Changing the phase-2 state machine contract or business error semantics.
Operator dashboards, full replay tooling, or final cost tuning.

module_boundaries.responsibility: Persist pending work items and expose a slot-based access pattern for scalable daily dispatch.
Drive evenly distributed dispatch execution across a 24-hour window by invoking one slot per schedule.
Query one dispatch slot, batch eligible records, and enqueue them to SQS FIFO.
Preserve same-provider ordering and provide scalable partitioned throughput without custom application sharding.
Remain intact from phase 2 and continue owning idempotency, retries, lifecycle closure, and provider execution once a message is dispatched.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: PendingRecordDispatchMetadata
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Additional metadata required to support scalable slot-based dispatch.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: DispatchSchedulerPayload
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Input that EventBridge Scheduler passes to the dispatch Lambda for a single slot window.

shape.targetDate: optional YYYY-MM-DD override for manual backfill

interfaces_and_contracts.name: DispatchLambdaOutput
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Operational summary for logs and manual validation.

interfaces_and_contracts.name: QueueMessageContract
interfaces_and_contracts.purpose: Phase-2-compatible message passed from dispatch Lambda to SQS FIFO.
interfaces_and_contracts.compatibility_rule: This message shape stays compatible with the existing orchestrator and state machine. No phase-2 downstream contract changes are introduced.

data_model_and_access_patterns.table_strategy: Keep tapi-pending-records as the pending-work system of record and extend it with slot-routing attributes instead of introducing a new table in phase 3.

new_index.name: dispatch-slot-index
new_index.primary_access_pattern: Query all records scheduled for one date-slot partition without scanning unrelated daily data.

slot_assignment_rule.algorithm: stable hash modulo slots per day
slot_assignment_rule.rationale: Ensures deterministic and approximately even distribution across the daily slot set while preserving provider grouping only at the SQS level.

read_pattern: Dispatch Lambda resolves the target date and slot id from the scheduler payload.
Dispatch Lambda performs Query on dispatch-slot-index for that partition only.
Dispatch Lambda paginates through the slot partition until exhausted.
write_pattern: Any writer that creates or seeds pending records must populate dispatch metadata at creation time.
Existing manual seed flows for tests can be updated with dispatch metadata in a later implementation task.

scheduler_strategy.design: Use recurring EventBridge Scheduler schedules distributed across the 24-hour window, one per dispatch slot.
scheduler_strategy.schedule_payload_rule: Each schedule passes its own slotId and slotsPerDay to the dispatch Lambda. The Lambda derives targetDate as today UTC unless an override is provided for manual backfill.
scheduler_strategy.flexible_time_window: OFF or equivalent strict timing behavior for predictable constant dispatch cadence.
why_scheduler: Avoids one daily monolithic dispatch invocation.
Makes throughput smoothing explicit and defendable.
Keeps dispatch cadence in infrastructure configuration instead of ad hoc code loops.

dispatch_lambda_behavior.responsibility: Read one slot partition and enqueue work items in SQS FIFO batches.
algorithm: Validate slotId and target date from payload.
Query dispatch-slot-index for the given date-slot partition.
Filter for records still in PENDING state.
Transform each eligible record into the existing queue message contract.
Publish messages using SendMessageBatch in groups of up to 10 entries.
Return summary counts for logs and validation.

runtime_limits.notes: 288 slots per day keeps the expected per-invocation load bounded enough to be defendable without custom continuation flow in the first implementation.

failure_handling: If a slot query or batch send fails, the schedule invocation is considered failed and can be retried by Scheduler policy.
Duplicate prevention after enqueue remains owned by the phase-2 operational flow via idempotency in Step Functions.
Dispatch Lambda does not mutate pending lifecycle states; it only selects eligible PENDING records and enqueues them.

sqs_high_throughput_strategy.message_group_rule: MessageGroupId remains PROVIDER#<providerId> so ordering is preserved per provider.
defendable_posture: We are explicitly not implementing manual shuffle-sharding in application code in this phase.
We rely on SQS FIFO High Throughput automatic partitioning based on the hash of MessageGroupId.
This preserves provider serialization while allowing AWS-managed horizontal partitioning of queue traffic.

unchanged_components: Queue message contract from dispatch Lambda to SQS.
Orchestrator Lambda responsibility to start one state machine execution per message.
Step Functions ownership of idempotency, retries, lifecycle closure, and final persistence.
Consumer Lambda responsibility as pure provider execution.
compatibility_guards: No additional fields are required by the downstream orchestrator for phase 3.
Phase-3 dispatch must continue producing one logical work item per queue message.
Provider isolation remains enforced at the SQS layer, not moved into Step Functions.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Large daily volume exceeds a single Lambda-friendly scan
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Prevented by design through slot partitioning and one-slot-per-schedule query.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Dispatch burst overloads queue or providers
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Reduced by 288 slot schedules distributed across the day and by SQS FIFO same-provider ordering.
Same-provider work remains serialized by MessageGroupId; global queue throughput scales through High Throughput partitioning for other providers.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A schedule invocation fails for one slot
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Scheduler retry policy handles the slot invocation; downstream idempotency prevents duplicate effective processing if the slot is retried.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: A record is no longer PENDING by the time its slot is processed
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Dispatch Lambda skips non-PENDING records and reports them as skipped in the summary.

failure_modes_and_edge_handling.case: Future scale requires stronger noisy-neighbor isolation than MessageGroupId hashing provides
failure_modes_and_edge_handling.handling: Explicitly deferred to a later phase where custom shuffle-sharding can be evaluated with real throughput evidence.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use EventBridge Scheduler as the temporal distribution driver.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: It makes distributed dispatch explicit and avoids relying on one daily execution.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use a slot-based GSI on tapi-pending-records instead of a monolithic daily query.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: It gives a defendable access pattern aligned to distributed dispatch.

dependency_and_library_decisions.decision: Use SQS FIFO High Throughput instead of manual shuffle-sharding in this phase.
dependency_and_library_decisions.rationale: This delegates partitioning to AWS while preserving provider ordering and keeping implementation risk lower.
Phase 2 already owns operational guarantees correctly, so phase 3 should scale dispatch without re-breaking lifecycle logic.

quality_gates: Unit tests cover slot payload parsing and deterministic slot assignment logic.
CDK synth proves creation of distributed schedules, dispatch-slot-index, and SQS FIFO High Throughput settings.
Manual AWS validation proves the dispatch Lambda only queries one slot partition and the downstream phase-2 workflow remains intact.
expected_test_scenarios: A given record identity always maps to the same dispatch slot for the same date.
Two different slots query different dispatchSlotPk values.
Dispatch Lambda publishes MessageGroupId as PROVIDER#<providerId> and stable deduplication ids.
CDK template includes dispatch-slot-index on tapi-pending-records.
CDK template includes one schedule per slot with the expected slotId payload.
CDK template enables FIFO High Throughput settings on the provider queue.
Manual dispatch of one slot produces queue messages that the existing orchestrator and state machine can process without contract changes.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Add deterministic slot-routing metadata to pending records.
tasks: Extend shared pending-record shape with dispatch metadata.
Add a slot computation utility based on stable hashing.
Add dispatch-slot-index to tapi-pending-records in CDK.
Update seed/test fixtures to include slot metadata where needed.
definition_of_done: Pending records can be queried by one date-slot partition.
Slot assignment is deterministic and testable.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Replace monolithic daily dispatch with distributed slot-based dispatch.
tasks: Refactor the dispatch Lambda to accept slot payloads and query one slot partition only.
Batch enqueue to SQS FIFO using stable deduplication ids and provider-based message groups.
Emit summary logs and counts for one slot execution.
Preserve the downstream queue message contract.
definition_of_done: One invocation handles exactly one date-slot partition.
Messages entering the queue remain phase-2 compatible.

phased_implementation_plan.goal: Distribute dispatch across the day and enable queue throughput posture.
tasks: Generate 288 EventBridge Scheduler schedules in CDK with strict 5-minute offsets.
Enable SQS FIFO High Throughput settings in CDK.
Retain queue DLQ and provider isolation semantics from phase 2.
Validate synth output and AWS deployment behavior.
definition_of_done: Dispatch is distributed across the day by infrastructure configuration.
Queue throughput posture is defendable without manual shuffle-sharding.

assumptions: A 5-minute slot cadence with 288 slots per day is a reasonable first implementation target for 1M+ records.
Writers of pending records can be updated to materialize dispatch metadata as part of phase-3 implementation.
The current provider queue and downstream state machine remain semantically correct once messages are enqueued.
Cost tuning and overflow continuation strategies beyond the first slot design can be deferred unless real test evidence proves them necessary.
